source.heading: ## ADRP-011: No-decision defaults for common UI states

obligations.text: No data: explicit empty-state action; loading: HTML/CSS shell before WASM; failure: visible recoverable error; offline: preserve local changes and label unsynced; version conflict: no overwrite, preserve edits and show reconciliation; unauthorized action: disabled/explained by F# capability; historical mode: visibly read-only; unknown semantics: preserve and block unsafe writes; reduced motion: disable nonessential animation.
No invented progress percentage or confidence score.

obligations.text: Offline startup: one documented command starts a populated Causa UI with no network or token; screen state and active fixture mode are visible.
Contract parity: identical valid fixture data yields identical domain reconstruction whether read from fixture or GitHub adapter.
Failure fidelity: malformed events fail closed; missing branch, 401/403, 404, 422, rate-limit, and timeout are classified correctly.
Stale-response regression: request B supersedes A; B completes first; late A cannot replace B.
Reverse completion order also tested.
Cache/auth regression: changing credentials invalidates relevant cached responses; an unauthorized request cannot be satisfied by stale cached success.
Visual checks: populated fixtures expose the complete UI-016 palette and labels; contrast and responsive checks pass.
Real integration: approved GitHub repository and pinned catalog are fetched over the network; all three historical investigation digests match.
Gate honesty: disconnected integration or missing secret reports BLOCKED, not PASS, while deterministic offline checks remain independently green.
Traceability: each PF requirement is mapped to an implementation test and evidence record; no future rehearsal may silently omit an applicable P0 requirement.

source.heading: ### R9.7 Deep links survive reload, sign-in and offline

When GitHub sign-in is needed, the application keeps the target, returns to it afterwards, and never returns outside the application.
A deep link to state that is already held locally opens offline, and its persistence state is shown truthfully.

**The verdict is computed, never written** (owner decision OD-INDY-7, [OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-24.md](OWNER-DECISIONS-2026-10-24.md)).
`tools/compute-acceptance-verdict.py` derives ACCEPTED, INCOMPLETE, BLOCKED, FAILED or INVALID from the ledger and independently supplied trust inputs.

It requires the candidate repository and trusted source SHA; the exact requirements baseline and its independently supplied SHA-256; a source checkout at the baseline commit; an externally pinned approvals file and SHA-256 plus the trusted operator identities; and a content-addressed evidence manifest, evidence directory and manifest SHA-256.
It exits 1 when the ledger's `accepted` flag or the report disagrees.
The report carries exactly one `<!-- acceptance-verdict: VERDICT -->` line, and no Verdict/Outcome line may claim acceptance the computation does not give.
The verifier opens every baseline source document at the pinned commit.
It compares every baseline P0 identity with the ledger, so deleting or downgrading an item cannot remove it from acceptance.

A scope change is effective only when it exactly matches an operator approval in the externally pinned approvals file and that approval's operator identity is named independently with `--trusted-operator-id`.
Agent-authored approvals in the ledger and untrusted operator identities are invalid.
Every PASS evidence path names a `causa.acceptance-evidence/1` JSON result in a `causa.acceptance-evidence-manifest/1` bundle.

The verifier checks the bundle's run and source identities, the bytes and SHA-256 of each result, the result's subject, status, command and exit code, required CI/deployment evidence types, and independent defect review evidence.
Missing, stale, altered or cross-run evidence is INVALID.

Digest pinning establishes integrity; authentication of the pins remains the responsibility of the trusted CI artifact, protected reference, Dokimos attestation or independent verifier supplying them.
A rehearsal's CI runs the structural and independent-verdict regression suites on every push and pull request.
This repository does not claim that the job is non-bypassable unless repository rules independently require it.
There is no ledger-local exclusion path: a P0 requirement leaves the verdict only through an externally pinned operator approval bound to the exact baseline.

obligations.text: Every screen and every addressable entity has a canonical URL (R9.6–R9.10, P34.15–P34.20; the portfolio standard is Praxis SAF-URL-1..10).
Pasting a copied URL into another browser opens the same view, after GitHub sign-in when needed.
The rules:
**Hash routes.** The route follows `#/` in `index.html#/...`, with relative links and no `<base href>`, so a reloaded deep link never 404s on GitHub Pages (D-203, Limen DF-LIMEN-2026-0006).
**IDs.** Every `{...Id}` is the entity's GUID (`FSHARP-TYPE-SHAPES.md`); `{branchId}` is the counterfactual BranchId and `{version}` is an aggregate version (`int`).
No other identifier, and no evidence content, appears in a URL.
**Repository.** Investigation routes carry the persistence repository as the `repo` query parameter (`owner/name`), so the link resolves in another browser (OQ-048).
**Version.** `at` (`int`) on any investigation-scoped route opens that view as of an aggregate version, visibly read-only (S14).
Without it the view shows the current version.
**Canonical form.** The canonical URL holds declared parameters only, in the order listed, with defaults omitted, sets sorted and de-duplicated, and `%20` with upper-case hex.
**History.** Moving between rows of the table, or to another entity, pushes history.
Changing a query parameter of the current row replaces it.
**Missing targets.** An unknown ID, an unreadable repository, or data not available offline shows not found, not permitted or unavailable offline with a way back, never another record (P34.19).
A superseded entity shows as superseded.
**Inventory.** `.echelon/routes.json` (`echelon.routes/v1`) lists exactly these routes and is regenerated from the route table (Limen `Inventory.render`).
**Copy link.** Screens marked ✓ offer a Copy link action that copies the canonical URL.
Every investigation-scoped pattern below is under `/investigations/{investigationId}`, written `…`.
| Screen | Route pattern | Query parameters (default) | Copy link |
| Home (investigation list) | `/` | `q` string; `status` set; `sort` enum `updated`/`title` (`updated`); `page` int (1) | |
| S01 Investigation Start | `/investigations/new` | `profile` string | |
| S02 Investigation Workspace | `/investigations/{investigationId}` | `repo`; `at`; `tab` enum (`overview`) | ✓ |
| S03 Hypothesis Battlefield | `…/hypotheses` | `repo`; `at`; `status` set; `sort` enum (`support`) | ✓ |
| S04 Hypothesis Detail | `…/hypotheses/{hypothesisId}` | `repo`; `at`; `tab` enum (`predictions`) | ✓ |
| S05 Evidence Capture | `…/evidence/new` | `repo`; `kind` enum | |

| S08 Unknown / Assumption / Contradiction | `…/unknowns/{unknownId}`, `…/assumptions/{assumptionId}`, `…/contradictions/{contradictionId}` | `repo`; `at` | ✓ |
| S09 Action / Experiment Designer | `…/actions/new`, `…/actions/{actionId}` | `repo`; `at` | ✓ |

obligations.text: The interface MUST have a deliberate, visibly colored Causa identity, not an effectively monochrome black/gray/white presentation.
Use these initial canonical palette values:
| Deep navy | Deep navy | `#14283F` | Primary navigation, masthead, structural emphasis |
| Teal | Teal | `#087F8C` | Primary investigation actions, active selection and positive workflow emphasis |
| Amber | Amber | `#E9A23B` | Unresolved unknowns, pending review and attention |
| Coral | Coral | `#D66B58` | Contradictions, material conflicts and critical investigation alerts |
| Soft ivory | Soft ivory | `#F5F3ED` | Main workspace surface and light backgrounds |
All colors MUST be mapped to named, semantic Forma theme tokens, not scattered hardcoded CSS declarations.
Use Forma components for surfaces, controls, states and focus treatment.

Ensure WCAG AA contrast for normal text (4.5:1), large text (3:1), and relevant non-text indicators (3:1).
Do not convey lifecycle, confidence, danger, verification or sync status through color alone: pair color with text and/or icons, and distinguish causal semantics from decorative accents.
Use the same token semantics across dashboard, investigation views, timeline, causal graph, evidence inspector, report and startup shell.
Print/Folio output MUST remain legible in grayscale.

Acceptance MUST include actual screenshots from the deployed exact SHA at desktop, iPad portrait/landscape and mobile sizes, plus automated token presence and contrast checks, keyboard focus checks, reduced-motion checks and independent visual review.
Verify that navy, teal, amber, coral and ivory appear in appropriate populated states; absence of data must not force a misleading status color.

Default labels: "Investigations" instead of "Historical investigations"; "Opening investigation" instead of "Fetching and validating the investigation"; "Status" instead of "Expected lifecycle"; "Investigation history" instead of "Replayed state"; "Explore changes" instead of "Open a sandbox copy"; "Apply change to draft" instead of "Ask the engine" when that is the actual action; "Change history" instead of "Engine decisions"; and "Discard draft" instead of "Discard the sandbox".
The wording MUST remain accurate to read-only, ephemeral, unsaved, and persisted states: never imply a draft was saved or a change was applied to the authoritative investigation when it was not.
Technical codes and provider details belong in Administration, except where needed in an explicitly requested technical detail view.
Preserve precise provenance and domain-specific terms where material.

requirements.title: Runtime diagnostics for the .NET WebAssembly engine

source.heading: ## WASM-DIAG-001: Runtime diagnostics for the .NET WebAssembly engine

obligations.text: The build MUST provide a diagnostics configuration of the .NET WebAssembly engine that enables Microsoft's EventPipe diagnostics (EnableDiagnostics, EventSourceSupport and MetricsSupport), so that managed heap dumps, CPU samples and metrics can be collected with the runtime's documented browser APIs.
The diagnostics configuration MUST NOT be the deployed production build.

A runtime failure MUST be capturable with browser developer tools, including the JavaScript and WebAssembly call stack of the failure, using an unstripped native runtime or its symbol map so that WebAssembly frames can be named.
Managed memory diagnostics MUST include heap dumps and garbage-collection activity before and after the failing operation where the runtime supports them.
Runtime performance profiling MUST be available through EventPipe CPU sampling or browser performance profiling, and each capture MUST record its duration and the operation it covers.
Exceptions and runtime failures MUST be captured with the exception type, message and stack, and the engine's state after the failure (usable or stopped) MUST be recorded.

Every diagnostic record MUST identify the .NET SDK, runtime and WebAssembly workload versions, the build configuration and execution mode (interpreter or AOT, and runtime options), the browser name and version, and the exact source commit.
Diagnostic evidence MUST be reproducible: the inputs, the build variant and the commands that produced it MUST be recorded so that another person can repeat the capture and obtain comparable results.

Diagnostic artifacts MUST be handled as sensitive: they MUST NOT contain credentials or tokens, MUST be scanned for token-shaped strings before they are uploaded or published, and MUST NOT be kept in public locations longer than needed.

Where practical, the capture and its checks MUST run automatically in CI, on a branch or workflow that does not affect the acceptance pipeline; where automation is not practical, the reason MUST be recorded.
